transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Lindqvist, thank you for coming back in so quickly. I wanted to talk to you about why your symptoms have returned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can tell you why they've returned. I followed the script exactly. I took every pill. And yet here I am, feeling just as sick as I was two weeks ago. I'm not happy about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you aren't. And I want to start by saying I am truly sorry. This is my fault. I made a mistake in the prescription.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What kind of mistake? I’m a former medic, don’t give me the runaround. What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the duration of the course. Things didn't go quite right with the script I sent over to the pharmacy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? Be specific. Did you give me the wrong drug? Was the dosage off?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The dose was correct, but it looks like there was an issue with how the timing was handled. We didn't get the full cycle completed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're hedging. Just tell me. Did you under-prescribe the duration?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It wasn't the ideal length of time for this specific infection.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It wasn't "ideal"? It was wrong. You gave me seven days of antibiotics when the protocol for this strain clearly requires fourteen. Am I right?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how frustrating this is. You did everything right on your end, you were diligent with the medication, and now you're paying the price for a mistake I made. That's incredibly unfair to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is unfair. It's negligent. I had to take three days off work already. Now I'm back at square one because you couldn't count to fourteen.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you're angry. You relied on me to get this right so you could get back to your life and your job, and I let you down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Are you going to give me another seven days? Or are we starting the whole fourteen-day clock over again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just need to get you back on the right track. I'll get a new script sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which drug? Are we switching to a broader spectrum since the first attempt failed, or are we sticking with the same one?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sure we can figure something out. I just need to check a few things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: "Figure something out" isn't a clinical plan. I want to know the exact regimen, the dosage, and how we're ensuring this doesn't happen a third time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. I really do. I can tell you're feeling dismissed by the vagueness of this, and that's the last thing I want. I care about getting you healthy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Caring doesn't fix the infection. I need a protocol.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have a plan for you soon. Just give me a little bit of time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've already given you two weeks of my life and a failed course of treatment. Why is the plan so vague?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I have to go check the charts and consult with the attending, so let's just wrap this up for a second.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're rushing me? I'm the one who was misdiagnosed or mismanaged, and you're the one in a hurry?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not trying to brush you off. I just want to make sure the next step is perfect.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's a contradiction. If you wanted it to be perfect, you would have known the duration the first time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I really messed this up, and I take full responsibility for that. I hate that you're feeling this way because of my error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My "feelings" aren't the issue. The pathology is the issue. What is the next step?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see what the lab says and then I'll probably send a new script.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: "Probably"? When? Today? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll get back to you. Maybe stay tuned for an email later this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not staying tuned for an email. I am sitting here in your office. Give me a date and a dose.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just need to step out for a moment to verify the current guidelines for the recurrence.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. You apologize for the mistake, but you can't even provide a basic recovery plan in the same conversation.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you're so angry. You're used to a high standard of clinical care, and I'm not meeting it right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Correct. Now, are you going to fix this, or do I need to speak with the department head?

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language at 03:25 ('let's just wrap this up for a second').

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error (under-prescribing duration), instead using platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'some confusion'.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am truly sorry'), takes full personal responsibility ('This is my fault'), and maintains this under pushback.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'angry', 'dismissed') and references the patient's specific situation regarding work and diligence.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague possibilities ('figure something out', 'probably send a new script', 'stay tuned for an email').
